mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the discount rate for equity cash flows, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day SPX returns remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.0%, it signals an economic slowdown that triggers a flight to quality and safe-haven assets, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises above 4.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: When HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% from prior month, the 20-day SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, which depress equity valuations and lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles (as defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% and the Fed not cutting rates for 3 consecutive months), the 60-day SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity and strong corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC between INDPRO and 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1500 thousand units, it signals a contraction in the housing market that reduces consumer confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST is below 1500 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a deteriorating labor market, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and PAYEMS declines > 0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and PAYEMS declines > 0.5% from prior month, the 20-day SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in retail sales (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion (as defined by GDP growth > 2.5% and unemployment below 4.5%), the 60-day SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS declines > 0.5% from prior month over a 3-year rolling window.
